boards.title: 10 Late-Night Runs That Explain Duke University
boards.description: Navigate Durham after dark with these essential late-night destinations, from on-campus study hubs to iconic off-campus eateries that define the Duke student experience.

cards.title: Cosmic Cantina
cards.subtitle: Ninth Street District
cards.notes: Climb the stairs to this Ninth Street staple for burritos and quesadillas. It is a primary late-night destination for students, remaining open until 4:00 AM daily.
cards.short_summary: A long-standing Mexican eatery on Ninth Street known for its late-night hours and rooftop patio.
cards.evidence_claim: Cosmic Cantina is open until 4:00 AM every day and is a popular late-night spot for students.
cards.access_notes: Open daily from 11:00 AM to 4:00 AM.

cards.title: Pitchfork's
cards.subtitle: McClendon Tower
cards.notes: Located in McClendon Tower, this campus cafe serves breakfast all day and late-night meals, often operating until 3:00 AM for students on West Campus.
cards.short_summary: An on-campus dining location in McClendon Tower offering late-night food options and 24/7 access during peak periods.
cards.evidence_claim: Pitchfork's is a late-night dining option on campus, often cited as being open until 3:00 AM.
cards.access_notes: Typically open late night until 3:00 AM during academic terms.

cards.title: Waffle House
cards.subtitle: Ninth Street
cards.notes: A reliable 24-hour spot on Ninth Street for breakfast classics. It serves as a quiet study alternative or a post-library meal destination for the Duke community.
cards.short_summary: A 24-hour diner located on Ninth Street near East Campus, popular for late-night breakfast.
cards.evidence_claim: The Waffle House on Ninth Street is open 24 hours a day, 7 days a week.
cards.access_notes: Open 24 hours daily.

cards.title: Cook Out
cards.subtitle: Shannon Road
cards.notes: Drive to this North Carolina classic for milkshakes and trays. The Shannon Road location is a frequent late-night stop, closing at 3:00 AM or later.
cards.short_summary: A regional fast-food chain famous for its extensive milkshake menu and late-night 'trays'.
cards.evidence_claim: Cook Out locations in Durham typically close between 3:00 AM and 4:00 AM.
cards.access_notes: Open until 3:00 AM Sunday-Thursday and 4:00 AM Friday-Saturday.

cards.title: Perkins Library
cards.subtitle: West Campus
cards.notes: The primary research library on West Campus. During the academic year, it offers extended hours, often remaining open until midnight or later for student study.
cards.short_summary: Duke's main library, providing late-night study spaces and resources for students.
cards.evidence_claim: Perkins Library offers extended hours until midnight or 3:00 AM during peak academic periods.
cards.access_notes: Hours vary by term; typically open until midnight or 3:00 AM Sunday-Thursday during semesters.

cards.title: McDonald's
cards.subtitle: Bryan Center
cards.notes: Conveniently located in the Bryan Center on West Campus, this McDonald's provides a familiar late-night food option for students studying nearby.
cards.short_summary: An on-campus McDonald's located in the Bryan Center, serving students late into the night.
cards.evidence_claim: The Bryan Center McDonald's is a designated late-night dining option on the Duke campus.
cards.access_notes: Open late; check current campus dining hours for specific closing times.

cards.title: Devil's Krafthouse
cards.subtitle: Brodhead Center
cards.notes: Located in the basement of the Brodhead Center, this venue offers a pub-style menu and is a popular late-night gathering spot, often open until midnight.
cards.short_summary: A campus eatery in the Brodhead Center known for its late-night food and social atmosphere.
cards.evidence_claim: Devil's Krafthouse is open until midnight and serves a late-night menu.
cards.access_notes: Typically open until midnight daily.

cards.title: Loop Pizza Grill
cards.subtitle: Bryan Center
cards.notes: A West Campus favorite in the Bryan Center, serving pizza, burgers, and shakes. It remains open until midnight, catering to late-night cravings.
cards.short_summary: A casual dining spot on West Campus offering a variety of late-night food options until midnight.
cards.evidence_claim: Loop Pizza Grill at Duke University is open until 12:00 AM daily.
cards.source_title: Loop Pizza Grill - Duke University - Discover Durham
cards.access_notes: Open daily from 11:00 AM to 12:00 AM.

cards.title: Enzo's Pizza Co.
cards.subtitle: Erwin Road
cards.notes: Located near campus on Erwin Road, Enzo's is a go-to for late-night pizza delivery or carryout, with weekend hours extending until 11:00 PM or later.
cards.short_summary: A local pizza shop near Duke's West Campus popular for its specialty pies and late-night availability.
cards.evidence_claim: Enzo's Pizza Co. on Erwin Road is open until 11:00 PM on Fridays and Saturdays.
cards.access_notes: Open until 10:00 PM Sun-Thu and 11:00 PM Fri-Sat.

cards.title: The Perk
cards.subtitle: Perkins Library
cards.notes: Commonly known as 'The Perk,' this glass-walled pavilion attached to Perkins Library offers late-night study space and coffee during the academic year.
cards.short_summary: A popular sunlit study space and cafe attached to Perkins Library that stays open late for students.
cards.evidence_claim: The von der Heyden Pavilion (The Perk) offers extended study hours until 3:00 AM during the semester.
cards.access_notes: Extended hours until 3:00 AM Sunday-Thursday during the academic semester.

boards.title: What the Campus Tour Skips: 10 Places Students Share With Each Other
boards.description: Discover the functional study hubs, quiet retreats, and social niches that Duke students use to navigate daily life on West and East Campus.

cards.title: Coffee and Views at Bella Union
cards.subtitle: McClendon Tower, West Campus
cards.notes: Head to the fourth floor of McClendon Tower for a laid-back cafe atmosphere. It is a favorite for late-night study sessions and watching campus snowfalls.
cards.short_summary: A student-favorite cafe and study spot located in McClendon Tower known for its cozy atmosphere and views.
cards.evidence_claim: Bella Union is described as a cozy, laid-back spot to get work done, located in McClendon Tower on West Campus.
cards.access_notes: Open to students; check Duke Dining for current cafe hours.

cards.title: Relaxation in The Oasis
cards.subtitle: Perkins Library, 4th Floor
cards.notes: Visit this quiet room for a mental break. It features yoga mats, puzzles, and white noise machines to help students de-stress during finals.
cards.short_summary: A dedicated wellness and relaxation room on the fourth floor of Perkins Library.
cards.evidence_claim: The Oasis is a room on the fourth floor of Perkins Library with yoga mats, puzzles, and comfy chairs for relaxation.
cards.source_title: Top 10 Hidden Study Spots at Duke University - Student Blogs
cards.access_notes: Located within Perkins Library; accessible during library operating hours.

cards.title: Silent Study in the Gothic Reading Room
cards.subtitle: Rubenstein Library, 2nd Floor
cards.notes: Experience the classic 'Gothic wonderland' vibe in this silent study space. It is ideal for deep focus amidst Duke's historic architecture.
cards.short_summary: A traditional, silent reading room located on the second floor of the Rubenstein Library.
cards.evidence_claim: The Gothic Reading Room is located on the second floor of Rubenstein Library and is noted as a perfect place for silent study.
cards.access_notes: Open during Rubenstein Library hours; strictly silent study.

cards.title: Build and Create at The Foundry
cards.subtitle: Gross Hall, Lower Level
cards.notes: Access 7,600 square feet of project space for engineering and entrepreneurship. It is the go-to spot for students building physical prototypes.
cards.short_summary: A large student makerspace and project area located in the basement of Gross Hall.
cards.evidence_claim: The Foundry is a 7,600-square-foot project space in the lower level of Gross Hall for students to build ideas.
cards.source_title: The Foundry -- Gross Hall - Duke Maps
cards.access_notes: Accessible to students; some equipment may require training or specific departmental access.

cards.title: Modern Hub at Wilkinson
cards.subtitle: West Campus
cards.notes: Utilize the numerous tables and chairs across several floors of this modern facility. The window-side seating offers great natural light for long sessions.
cards.short_summary: A modern engineering building with extensive open study areas and natural lighting.
cards.evidence_claim: The Wilkinson Engineering Building has many tables and chairs available for study across several floors.
cards.source_title: Top 10 Hidden Study Spots at Duke University - Student Blogs
cards.access_notes: Open to the Duke community; features multiple floors of seating.

cards.title: Quiet Corridors in French Family
cards.subtitle: Science Drive, West Campus
cards.notes: Find a quiet seat at the end of the long hallways or on benches in the main atrium. It is a massive space often overlooked for focused work.
cards.short_summary: A large science facility with quiet seating areas tucked away in its atriums and hallways.
cards.evidence_claim: The French Family Science Center features a giant hallway and atrium with benches and quiet seats for studying.
cards.source_title: Top 10 Hidden Study Spots at Duke University - Student Blogs
cards.access_notes: Public areas are accessible during building hours.

cards.title: Artistic Break at the Nasher
cards.subtitle: 2001 Campus Drive
cards.notes: Take advantage of free admission to browse the galleries or study in the cafe. It provides a sophisticated change of pace from traditional libraries.
cards.short_summary: Duke's art museum offering free admission and a cafe space suitable for a quiet break.
cards.evidence_claim: The Nasher Museum of Art offers free admission for all and includes a museum cafe and store.
cards.source_title: Plan Your Visit - Nasher Museum of Art
cards.access_notes: Free admission; closed on Mondays. Check website for current cafe hours.

cards.title: Melodic Study at Biddle
cards.subtitle: East Campus
cards.notes: Escape to the Biddle Music Building for a quieter alternative to West Campus libraries. It offers study spaces on both floors with a musical backdrop.
cards.short_summary: A specialized library on East Campus known for its quiet atmosphere and music collections.
cards.evidence_claim: The Biddle Music Building has library-based study locations on both floors.
cards.access_notes: Open during Music Library hours; located on East Campus.

cards.title: Social Hub at the Brodhead Center
cards.subtitle: 406 Chapel Drive, West Campus
cards.notes: Meet friends or find a niche in this central dining hub. With 13 restaurants and various lounges, it is the heart of student social life and dining.
cards.short_summary: The primary student dining and social center on West Campus, featuring diverse food options and seating.
cards.evidence_claim: The Brodhead Center (WU) is a great place to study or socialize, offering various spaces and 13 dining venues.
cards.access_notes: Open daily; check Duke Dining for specific restaurant hours.

cards.title: Gateway at Karsh Center
cards.subtitle: Duke University Road
cards.notes: Explore the modern events pavilion and meeting spaces at the campus entrance. It serves as a welcoming gateway with striking glass and stone architecture.
cards.short_summary: A modern complex at the entrance of West Campus featuring event spaces and a visitor cafe.
cards.evidence_claim: The Karsh Alumni and Visitors Center features a large events pavilion, meeting spaces, and a cafe.
cards.source_title: Karsh Alumni and Visitors Center - Duke Maps
cards.access_notes: Open to visitors and the Duke community; includes a cafe and exhibit areas.

boards.title: Zero Dollars: 10 Hangs That Cost Nothing
boards.description: Discover the best social spaces and activities at Duke University that require no admission fee or purchase, from historic gardens to iconic campus landmarks.

cards.title: Stroll the Historic Terraces
cards.subtitle: 55-acre public botanical garden
cards.notes: Walk through the Italianate terraces and Asiatic arboretum. Admission is free for all visitors daily from 8 a.m. until dusk.
cards.short_summary: A premier 55-acre public garden on campus featuring diverse floral displays and walking paths with no entry fee.
cards.evidence_claim: Admission to Sarah P. Duke Gardens is free for all visitors, though there is a fee for parking.
cards.access_notes: Open daily from 8 a.m. to dusk. Public access is free; parking is $2 per hour.

cards.title: Visit the Gothic Landmark
cards.subtitle: Iconic campus center and house of worship
cards.notes: Explore the soaring nave and stained glass of this neo-Gothic masterpiece. Public visiting hours are typically 10 a.m. to 8 p.m. daily.
cards.short_summary: The architectural centerpiece of West Campus, offering free public access for tours, reflection, and services.
cards.evidence_claim: Duke University Chapel is open to the public from 10 a.m. to 8 p.m. daily unless otherwise noted for private events.
cards.source_title: Plan a Visit | Duke University Chapel
cards.access_notes: Open daily 10 a.m. to 8 p.m. Check the online calendar for closures due to weddings or private ceremonies.

cards.title: Browse Contemporary Galleries
cards.subtitle: University art museum
cards.notes: View rotating exhibitions of contemporary and historical art. Admission is free for everyone, including the general public.
cards.short_summary: A major campus art museum featuring diverse collections and global exhibitions with free admission for all.
cards.evidence_claim: The Nasher Museum of Art offers free admission for all visitors.
cards.source_title: Plan Your Visit - Nasher Museum of Art at Duke University
cards.access_notes: Open Tuesday–Saturday 10 a.m. to 5 p.m. and Sunday 12 p.m. to 5 p.m. Closed Mondays.

cards.title: Walk the Gravel Loop
cards.subtitle: 1.7-mile perimeter trail
cards.notes: Join students and locals for a walk or jog along the historic stone wall. The gravel path is a popular social and exercise spot.
cards.short_summary: A scenic 1.7-mile gravel trail circling Duke's East Campus, popular for walking, running, and socializing.
cards.evidence_claim: The East Campus Wall and its 1.7-mile gravel pathway are open to the public for walking and jogging.
cards.source_title: New Entrances Added Along East Campus Wall | Duke Today
cards.access_notes: Publicly accessible 24/7; most popular during daylight hours.

cards.title: Socialize in the Student Hub
cards.subtitle: West Campus student union
cards.notes: Find a spot in the multi-level lounges or outdoor seating areas. This central hub is open for studying and gathering without a purchase.
cards.short_summary: The primary student gathering space on West Campus, offering extensive free seating and social areas.
cards.evidence_claim: The Brodhead Center (West Union) provides various lounge and study spaces that are open to the student community.
cards.access_notes: Open daily; late-night access is common for students with DukeCard. Public seating is available during building hours.

cards.title: Study in the Main Libraries
cards.subtitle: Primary campus library complex
cards.notes: Access vast study spaces and the Oasis relaxation room. Visitors can enter during public hours; students have 24-hour access.
cards.short_summary: Duke's main library complex offers diverse environments for study and research with free public entry during designated hours.
cards.evidence_claim: Members of the public are welcome to visit and use the Duke University Libraries during public hours.
cards.source_title: Public Access and Hours | Duke University Libraries
cards.access_notes: Public hours vary; DukeCard required for late-night and overnight access.

cards.title: Explore the Welcome Center
cards.subtitle: Campus entry and visitor hub
cards.notes: Visit the exhibition hall to learn about Duke's history. The center serves as a free starting point for campus tours and exploration.
cards.short_summary: A modern visitor center providing information and historical exhibits about the university with free admission.
cards.evidence_claim: The Karsh Alumni and Visitors Center is a space for alumni and visitors to explore Duke's history and campus.
cards.access_notes: Open to the public during business hours, typically Monday–Friday 8:30 a.m. to 5 p.m.

cards.title: Hang Out in the Bryan Center
cards.subtitle: Student activities and arts complex
cards.notes: Find comfortable seating and student organization hubs. It is a central spot for meeting friends or catching a free student performance.
cards.short_summary: A multi-purpose student center housing lounges, theaters, and student services with free common areas.
cards.evidence_claim: The Bryan Center offers various study and social spaces that are free for student use.
cards.access_notes: Open daily; building hours extend late for student activities.

cards.title: Study in Silent Grandeur
cards.subtitle: Historic Rubenstein Library space
cards.notes: Experience one of the most beautiful study spots on campus. This room in the Rubenstein Library is dedicated to quiet study and is free to access.
cards.short_summary: A stunning, historic reading room in the Rubenstein Library known for its silent atmosphere and Gothic architecture.
cards.evidence_claim: The Gothic Reading Room is a designated study space available for students and visitors during library hours.
cards.access_notes: Open during Rubenstein Library hours. Strict quiet policy enforced.

cards.title: Hike the Shepherd Nature Trail
cards.subtitle: University-owned research forest
cards.notes: Explore miles of trails open for hiking and running. The Shepherd Nature Trail is a popular, easy loop accessible for free.
cards.short_summary: A vast research forest offering over 7,000 acres of land with numerous trails open to the public for recreation.
cards.evidence_claim: Duke Forest is open to the public for low-impact recreation like hiking and running on designated trails.
cards.access_notes: Open daily from sunrise to sunset. Visitors must stay on designated trails.

boards.title: Claimed by 9am: 10 Study Spots Worth Showing Up Early For
boards.description: From the silent gothic halls of Rubenstein to the collaborative labs of the Wilkinson Building, Duke offers a diverse range of environments for focused research and group projects.

cards.title: Gothic Reading Room
cards.subtitle: Rubenstein Library, Floor 2
cards.notes: Enter this silent zone for focused work. No food or drink is permitted except water. Outlets are available at every table under historic gothic arches.
cards.short_summary: A silent, architecturally stunning study hall in the Rubenstein Library dedicated to absolute quiet.
cards.evidence_claim: The Gothic Reading Room is a silent study space where noise, eating, and drinking (except water) are prohibited, and outlets are available at each table.
cards.source_title: Gothic Reading Room – Academic Resource Center - Duke ARC
cards.access_notes: Open Monday-Friday 8am-5pm for silent study.

cards.title: The Edge
cards.subtitle: Bostock Library, Floor 1
cards.notes: Use the Jones Open Lab for collaborative team-based research. The space features mobile furniture, writable wall surfaces, and data visualization labs.
cards.short_summary: A collaborative hub for interdisciplinary and data-driven research located on the first floor of Bostock Library.
cards.evidence_claim: The Edge provides collaborative space with writable surfaces, mobile furniture, and project rooms for group research.
cards.source_title: Spaces in the Edge | Duke University Libraries
cards.access_notes: Reservable project rooms available for groups of 2-12 people.

cards.title: Brodhead Center
cards.subtitle: West Union
cards.notes: Head to the upper floors for a quieter atmosphere. This central hub offers plenty of seating, reliable Wi-Fi, and easy access to campus dining.
cards.short_summary: A multi-level student center with varied noise levels and extensive seating for social or focused study.
cards.evidence_claim: The Brodhead Center offers various seating options including tables, benches, and couches, with upper floors being quieter for focused work.
cards.source_title: Brodhead Center (WU) – Academic Resource Center - Duke ARC
cards.access_notes: Open 8am-10pm daily; moderate noise level on lower floors.

cards.title: Divinity School Library Zoom Pods
cards.subtitle: Gray Building, BQ-BR Level
cards.notes: Book one of five sound-proof pods for private video calls or online classes. These reservable booths are located upstairs in the Divinity Library.
cards.short_summary: Private, sound-proof booths designed for individual video conferencing and online meetings.
cards.evidence_claim: The Divinity Library has five 'Zoom Pods' on the BQ-BR level that students can book for online classes and meetings.
cards.source_title: Hybrid Students | Duke Divinity School Library
cards.access_notes: Reservable online; open to the larger University community.

cards.title: Medical Center Library Cubicles
cards.subtitle: Seeley G. Mudd Building, Level 2R
cards.notes: Find individual quiet study cubicles on the second and third floors. These spaces are available for Duke-affiliated students on a first-come basis.
cards.short_summary: Individual quiet study stations located within the Duke University Medical Center Library.
cards.evidence_claim: Individual quiet study cubicles are available on Level 2R and Level 3 of the Medical Center Library for Duke-affiliated users.
cards.source_title: Book A Study Room or Cubicle | Duke University Medical Center Library Online
cards.access_notes: Cubicles have no time limit but are subject to a 15-minute grace period for arrival.

cards.title: Wilkinson Building Garage Labs
cards.subtitle: Pratt School of Engineering
cards.notes: Utilize the main floor Garage Labs for hands-on design and active learning. This LEED-certified facility is a hub for engineering entrepreneurship.
cards.short_summary: Modern, hands-on design spaces for engineering students located on the main floor of the Wilkinson Building.
cards.evidence_claim: The Wilkinson Building features 'Garage Labs' on the main floor for hands-on design and active-learning classrooms.
cards.source_title: Visit | Duke Pratt School of Engineering
cards.access_notes: Open for student use; adjacent to Bseisu Coffee Bar.

cards.title: Goodson Law Library Reading Room
cards.subtitle: Duke Law School, Level 3
cards.notes: Access twelve public computer terminals in this spacious reading room. Duke Card holders can use the space for research and quiet study.
cards.short_summary: A professional research environment with public computer terminals and extensive legal collections.
cards.evidence_claim: The Goodson Law Library Reading Room has twelve computer terminals available for visitors and students during public access hours.
cards.source_title: Public | Duke University School of Law
cards.access_notes: Public access may be limited to Duke Card holders during certain periods; check current hours.

cards.title: Music Library
cards.subtitle: Biddle Music Building, East Campus
cards.notes: Study across two floors of this specialized library. It offers a quiet alternative on East Campus while Lilly Library is under renovation.
cards.short_summary: A quiet, two-story library on East Campus specializing in music resources and study areas.
cards.evidence_claim: The Music Library in the Biddle Music Building has study spaces on both floors and is an alternative for East Campus students.
cards.access_notes: Typically open 11am-3pm during summer; check semester hours for extended access.

cards.title: Bella Union
cards.subtitle: McClendon Tower, West Campus
cards.notes: Grab a coffee and find a seat in this cozy, laid-back environment. It is a popular spot for casual study and social work sessions.
cards.short_summary: A relaxed cafe-style study environment located in McClendon Tower on West Campus.
cards.evidence_claim: Bella Union is described as a cozy, laid-back spot to get work done on West Campus.
cards.source_title: Bella Union – Academic Resource Center - Duke ARC
cards.access_notes: Open for casual study; food and drink available for purchase.

cards.title: Interview Room Perkins 130
cards.subtitle: Perkins Library, Floor 1
cards.notes: Reserve this specialized room for phone or video interviews. It includes a dedicated telephone line and a quiet, professional setting.
cards.short_summary: A reservable private room in Perkins Library equipped for professional interviews and calls.
cards.evidence_claim: Perkins 130 is a reservable interview room with a telephone (919-660-5959) located on the first floor.
cards.source_title: Find Library Spaces | Duke University Libraries
cards.access_notes: Reservable online via the Duke Libraries calendar.

boards.title: 10 Blocks Off Campus, One Reason Each
boards.description: Explore the distinct corridors and districts surrounding Duke University, from the historic Ninth Street to the industrial-chic American Tobacco Campus.

cards.title: Ninth Street
cards.subtitle: Ninth Street Corridor
cards.notes: Visit the Regulator Bookshop for local reads or grab a scratch-made donut at Monuts in this historic district just blocks from East Campus.
cards.short_summary: The primary off-campus commercial hub for Duke students, featuring local bookstores, cafes, and independent retail.
cards.evidence_claim: Ninth Street is described as the social center of off-campus Duke life and a walkable strip packed with restaurants and shops.
cards.source_title: Neighborhood Guide: Ninth Street - nearDuke Off-Campus Guide
cards.access_notes: Public street with various business hours; Monuts is open until 9:00 PM Tuesday-Saturday.

cards.title: Brightleaf Square
cards.subtitle: West Main Street
cards.notes: Explore repurposed tobacco warehouses housing Rose's Noodles and Jeni's Splendid Ice Creams in this historic Romanesque brick district.
cards.short_summary: A historic district of renovated tobacco warehouses featuring upscale dining, retail, and courtyard spaces.
cards.evidence_claim: Brightleaf Square is a main hub for restaurants and shopping in the west end of downtown Durham, close to Duke's East Campus.
cards.access_notes: Open daily; courtyard is accessible to the public; individual business hours vary.

cards.title: Erwin Road
cards.subtitle: Erwin Road Corridor
cards.notes: Walk to Enzo's Pizza or Chipotle from the Lofts at Lakeview in this high-density residential area adjacent to Duke Medical Center.
cards.short_summary: A major thoroughfare bordering West Campus and the Medical Center, lined with student-oriented apartments and fast-casual dining.
cards.evidence_claim: Erwin Road is a primary residential area for Duke students, featuring complexes like Lofts at Lakeview and various dining options.
cards.access_notes: Public thoroughfare; businesses typically open until 10:00 PM or later.

cards.title: Broad Street
cards.subtitle: Broad Street Corridor
cards.notes: Grab a coffee at Joe Van Gogh or shop at the local Whole Foods in this quieter alternative to the Ninth Street bustle.
cards.short_summary: A commercial corridor parallel to Ninth Street offering local coffee shops and essential grocery services.
cards.evidence_claim: Broad Street is home to Joe Van Gogh coffee and is a popular weekend stop for students and locals.
cards.access_notes: Public street; Joe Van Gogh is a popular study spot for students.

cards.title: Foster Street
cards.subtitle: Central Park District
cards.notes: Visit the Durham Farmers Market on Saturday mornings or explore the Durham Food Hall in this vibrant arts and recreation district.
cards.short_summary: The heart of Durham's Central Park district, known for its weekly farmers market and community events.
cards.evidence_claim: Foster Street is the location of Durham Central Park and the Durham Farmers Market, serving as a community hub.
cards.access_notes: Farmers Market open Saturdays 8am-12pm; park is open daily.

cards.title: Geer Street
cards.subtitle: Geer Street Corridor
cards.notes: Check out the murals at GeerHouse or grab a coffee at Cocoa Cinnamon in this rapidly developing industrial-style neighborhood.
cards.short_summary: A trendy district north of downtown featuring historic service stations converted into cafes and restaurants.
cards.evidence_claim: Geer Street features local favorites like Cocoa Cinnamon and Geer Street Garden, often housed in repurposed historic buildings.
cards.access_notes: Public street; Cocoa Cinnamon is a popular student hangout.

cards.title: American Tobacco Campus
cards.subtitle: Blackwell Street
cards.notes: Walk along the man-made river or catch a Durham Bulls game next door at this massive historic factory redevelopment.
cards.short_summary: A premier mixed-use destination featuring offices, restaurants, and the iconic Lucky Strike water tower.
cards.evidence_claim: The American Tobacco Campus is a historic redevelopment with over a million square feet of space, including restaurants and green space.
cards.access_notes: Open to the public 24/7; security on-site; individual business hours vary.

cards.title: West Main Street
cards.subtitle: Downtown Main Street
cards.notes: Dine at local staples like Devine's Restaurant or explore the shops connecting the Brightleaf District to the city center.
cards.short_summary: The primary east-west artery of downtown Durham, connecting Duke's East Campus to the central business district.
cards.evidence_claim: West Main Street is a key corridor featuring long-standing businesses like Devine's and connecting major districts.
cards.access_notes: Public thoroughfare; Devine's is open late for sports viewing.

cards.title: University Hill
cards.subtitle: University Drive
cards.notes: View the UHILL Walls, one of the largest mural collections in the Southeast, while visiting local eateries in this mixed-use development.
cards.short_summary: A modern mixed-use development known for its extensive mural art and diverse food and drink options.
cards.evidence_claim: University Hill features over 35 murals and 8+ food and drink establishments within a 300,000 square foot development.
cards.access_notes: Publicly accessible mural walk; retail hours vary.

cards.title: Gregson Street
cards.subtitle: Trinity Park / Downtown
cards.notes: Visit The Can Opener food truck park near the famous low-clearance bridge for local eats and outdoor games.
cards.short_summary: A corridor bordering Trinity Park featuring new community-focused dining concepts and the infamous 'Can Opener' bridge.
cards.evidence_claim: The Can Opener on Gregson Street is a food truck park offering a variety of local vendors and outdoor seating.
cards.access_notes: Open daily 7:00 AM - 10:00 PM; food truck hours may vary.

boards.title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
boards.description: From camping in a tent city for basketball tickets to celebrating victories with controlled bonfires, Duke University's traditions are deeply rooted in its Gothic campus and athletic spirit.

cards.title: Tenting in K-Ville
cards.subtitle: A Winter Campout for Basketball
cards.notes: Students camp in tents for weeks outside Cameron Indoor Stadium to secure tickets for the Duke-UNC game. Line monitors enforce strict occupancy rules and call random checks.
cards.short_summary: A multi-week student tent city established to secure admission to the annual home game against rival UNC.
cards.evidence_claim: Tenting has been a tradition at Duke for 40 years, with students camping in 'K-Ville' for 2-6 weeks leading up to the Duke-UNC game.
cards.source_title: K-Ville & The ARC Study Tent | Office of Undergraduate Education
cards.access_notes: The grassy area in front of Card Gym is accessible to students during the tenting season; specific rules apply to registered tenters.

cards.title: Victory Bench Burning
cards.subtitle: Post-Game Bonfire Celebrations
cards.notes: Following major basketball victories, specifically over UNC or for National Championships, students gather on the quad to burn wooden benches in a supervised bonfire.
cards.short_summary: A controlled bonfire tradition where students burn benches to celebrate significant basketball wins.
cards.evidence_claim: The A-Team burns a bench for men's and women's basketball victories over UNC and for National Championship wins, with student roles like stokers and extinguishers.
cards.access_notes: Occurs on the West Campus quads following specific major athletic victories.

cards.title: LDOC Celebration
cards.subtitle: The Ultimate End-of-Semester Festival
cards.notes: The final day of the spring semester features a massive campus-wide festival with daytime programming and a major concert organized by the Duke University Union.
cards.short_summary: A large-scale festival and concert held annually to mark the final day of the academic year.
cards.evidence_claim: LDOC is a major tradition featuring daytime programming, philanthropy, and a festival-like concert to celebrate the last day of classes.
cards.source_title: DUU Last Day of Classes Celebration | Duke University
cards.access_notes: The event is primarily for Duke students and takes place across various campus locations on the final day of spring classes.

cards.title: Midnight Breakfast
cards.subtitle: Late-Night Finals Fuel
cards.notes: During finals week, dining halls open late to serve breakfast food to students. It is a cherished tradition for first-years at the Marketplace on East Campus.
cards.short_summary: A late-night dining event during exam periods where students gather for breakfast food and a study break.
cards.evidence_claim: Midnight Breakfast is a tradition hosted each semester during the exam reading period, featuring a buffet of brunch foods at the Marketplace and Great Hall.
cards.access_notes: Held late at night during reading periods; free for first-years on the meal plan, others can pay with points or cash.

cards.title: The 5:00 PM Carillon
cards.subtitle: Daily Gothic Melodies
cards.notes: Every weekday at 5:00 PM, the 50-bell carillon in the Duke Chapel tower is played manually. On Fridays, the 'Dear Old Duke' alma mater is always included.
cards.short_summary: A daily musical performance from the Duke Chapel tower featuring a manual 50-bell carillon.
cards.evidence_claim: The carillon is played on weekdays at 5:00 p.m., and the Duke Alma Mater is played every Friday, a tradition started during Terry Sanford's presidency.
cards.access_notes: The music can be heard across West Campus; the recital occurs daily at 5:00 PM.

cards.title: The Cameron Crazies
cards.subtitle: The Sixth Man of Duke Basketball
cards.notes: Known for their coordinated cheers, blue body paint, and creative distractions, this student section is a defining element of the game-day experience at Cameron Indoor Stadium.
cards.short_summary: The highly energetic and organized student section for Duke basketball games.
cards.evidence_claim: The term 'Cameron Crazies' took root in 1986 to describe the raucous behavior of Duke students during home basketball games.
cards.access_notes: Access to the student section requires a student ID and often involves waiting in line or tenting.

cards.title: The Cascada Dance
cards.subtitle: A Modern Game-Day Ritual
cards.notes: During basketball games, the song 'Everytime We Touch' by Cascada triggers a specific coordinated dance and clap among students that has spread to other campus events.
cards.short_summary: A specific song and dance ritual performed by students during basketball games and university events.
cards.evidence_claim: The song 'Everytime We Touch' became a Duke tradition at basketball games, involving signature singing, clapping, and dancing.
cards.source_title: Traditions at Duke – Blue Devil Food for Thought
cards.access_notes: Performed by the student body during home basketball games and major social gatherings.

cards.title: FAC Move-In Day
cards.subtitle: High-Energy Welcome to East Campus
cards.notes: Upperclassmen known as FACs welcome new students by sprinting to cars and carrying all their belongings into dorms, creating a high-energy atmosphere for move-in.
cards.short_summary: A high-energy welcome tradition where student counselors assist first-years with moving into their dorms.
cards.evidence_claim: First-year advisory counselors (FAC) do most of the heavy lifting during move-in day, maintaining excited spirits to welcome new members of the community.
cards.source_title: Traditions at Duke – Blue Devil Food for Thought
cards.access_notes: Occurs annually on the official move-in day for first-year students on East Campus.

cards.title: The Spring Bloom
cards.subtitle: A Seasonal Campus Pilgrimage
cards.notes: Every spring, students and locals visit the Terrace Gardens to see the massive display of over 60,000 bulbs, a tradition of seasonal appreciation since the 1930s.
cards.short_summary: The annual spring blooming of tens of thousands of flower bulbs in the historic Terrace Gardens.
cards.evidence_claim: The horticulture team typically plants more than 60,000 bulbs annually for spring displays in the Terrace Gardens, including a sea of tulips.
cards.source_title: Nine Facts: Sarah P. Duke Gardens
cards.access_notes: The gardens are open to the public daily; the peak bloom typically occurs in late March or April.

cards.title: The Blue Devil Nickname
cards.subtitle: A Tribute to WWI Chasseurs Alpins
cards.notes: The university's nickname was chosen by students after WWI to honor the 'les Diables Bleus,' elite French alpine troops known for their distinctive blue uniforms.
cards.short_summary: The official university moniker inspired by elite French soldiers from World War I.
cards.evidence_claim: The Blue Devil nickname was chosen after World War I, inspired by the 'Chasseurs Alpins' (Blue Devils) of the French Army.
cards.source_title: Duke University Traditions - The Sports Historian
cards.access_notes: The nickname and mascot are visible at all university athletic and spirit events.

boards.title: Your First Weekend at Duke University, Shared as Cards
boards.description: Build a plausible under-21-safe first-weekend sequence, not a ranking. Give each card one role in the sequence and use evergreen places or recurring behaviors rather than one-time events. Be conservative about hours, access, and travel time unless directly sourced.

cards.title: Unpack on East Campus
cards.subtitle: The First-Year Home Base
cards.notes: Begin your journey where all first-years live. Meet your hallmates in the Georgian-style dorms and get settled into the residential community that defines the freshman experience.
cards.short_summary: The dedicated residential campus for all first-year Duke students.
cards.evidence_claim: All first-year students live together on East Campus to build a sense of solidarity and community.
cards.source_title: Your First Year - Duke Undergraduate Admissions
cards.access_notes: Restricted to residential students and authorized guests.

cards.title: First Breakfast at Marketplace
cards.subtitle: East Campus Dining Hall
cards.notes: Head to the East Campus Union for your first communal meal. It is a central hub for first-years to gather for breakfast and the signature weekend brunch.
cards.short_summary: The primary dining hall for first-year students located on East Campus.
cards.evidence_claim: Marketplace brunches create a sense of solidarity and community foundational to the Duke experience.
cards.source_title: Your First Year - Duke Undergraduate Admissions
cards.access_notes: Open daily; check Duke Dining for specific first-year meal plan hours.

cards.title: Ride the C1 to West Campus
cards.subtitle: The Campus Connector
cards.notes: Catch the frequent campus shuttle for the 1.2-mile trip to West Campus. It's the primary way students navigate between the Georgian and Gothic sections of the university.
cards.short_summary: The main transit route connecting East and West campuses.
cards.evidence_claim: The C1: West-East Bus is the recommended way to travel between campuses and is free for students.
cards.access_notes: Runs frequently throughout the day and late into the night during the academic year.

cards.title: Visit the Duke Chapel
cards.subtitle: Iconic Gothic Landmark
cards.notes: Step inside the center of West Campus to admire the neo-Gothic architecture. It serves as the site for the Opening Convocation that welcomes all new students.
cards.short_summary: The architectural centerpiece of Duke's West Campus.
cards.evidence_claim: The Chapel is open to the public from 10 am – 8 pm daily and hosts the Opening Convocation for first-years.
cards.source_title: Visiting & Camps - Coronavirus Response - Duke University
cards.access_notes: Open daily 10:00 AM to 8:00 PM unless a private event is scheduled.

cards.title: Lunch at West Union
cards.subtitle: The Brodhead Center
cards.notes: Explore 13 different food vendors in this modern dining hub. It's the social heart of West Campus where students gather for meals and study sessions.
cards.short_summary: A multi-vendor dining facility located on West Campus.
cards.evidence_claim: West Union features 13 different vendors offering fresh food for dining in or to-go.
cards.access_notes: Open daily; individual vendor hours vary.

cards.title: Stroll Through Duke Gardens
cards.subtitle: 55 Acres of Botanic Beauty
cards.notes: Walk through the Terraces and Asiatic Arboretum. This world-class garden is located right on campus and offers a peaceful escape for new students.
cards.short_summary: A renowned public botanic garden located on the Duke University campus.
cards.evidence_claim: The gardens are open 8 a.m. to sunset 365 days a year with free admission.
cards.access_notes: Open daily from 8:00 AM to sunset.

cards.title: Explore the Nasher Museum
cards.subtitle: Campus Art Destination
cards.notes: View contemporary art collections just a short walk from the gardens. Admission is free for everyone, making it an easy cultural stop during your first weekend.
cards.short_summary: Duke University's art museum featuring global contemporary works.
cards.evidence_claim: The Nasher Museum of Art offers free admission for all visitors.
cards.source_title: Plan Your Visit - Nasher Museum of Art at Duke University
cards.access_notes: Open Tuesday-Saturday 10 AM - 5 PM, Sunday 12 PM - 5 PM; closed Mondays.

cards.title: Browse the Bryan Center
cards.subtitle: Student Union & Box Office
cards.notes: Visit the student union to find the University Box Office, theaters, and the Duke Store. It's a key spot for getting involved in campus life.
cards.short_summary: The main student union building on West Campus.
cards.evidence_claim: The Bryan Center is Duke's student union and home to performance theaters and the university box office.
cards.access_notes: General building access is open daily; specific office hours vary.

cards.title: See Cameron Indoor Stadium
cards.subtitle: Home of the Blue Devils
cards.notes: Walk by the legendary basketball arena and the adjacent Basketball Museum. Check for tour availability to see the court and championship trophies up close.
cards.short_summary: The historic home arena for Duke University basketball.
cards.evidence_claim: Guided tours of Cameron Indoor Stadium and the Duke Basketball Museum must be booked 48 hours in advance.
cards.access_notes: Closed except for athletics events and scheduled tours.

cards.title: Active Hour at Wilson Rec
cards.subtitle: West Campus Fitness
cards.notes: End your weekend with a workout or a game of basketball. This 99,000-square-foot facility is the larger of Duke's two main recreation centers.
cards.short_summary: A large-scale fitness and recreation facility on West Campus.
cards.evidence_claim: Wilson Recreation Center is a 99,000 square foot facility on West Campus available to students.
cards.source_title: Wilson Recreation Center | Recreation & Physical Education
cards.access_notes: Open daily; check the MyRec app for current student hours.
